# Mezcalómano

> Mezcalómano is an agave education brand. We make the Discovery Deck, a deck of playing cards that introduces 40 kinds of mezcal and the agaves behind them, and we publish a free agave directory and a short-reads series called Small Pours.

## Key facts

- Product: THE DISCOVERY DECK, 40 agave species, $29.99, sold at https://shop.mezcalomano.com/products/discovery-deck. Pre-orders ship from November 30, 2026. US addresses only for now.
- Seller of record: That's SaaS Limited, a UK company, trading as Mezcalómano. Public email: hola@mezcalomano.com.
- Espadín made up about 85% of certified mezcal in 2025 (COMERCAM, Informe Estadístico 2026).
- Our approach is agave first: we describe taste, agave and common names, not brands.

- [Mezcal Cocktails That Still Taste of the Agave](https://mezcalomano.com/small-pours/mezcal-cocktails-that-taste-of-agave): Four simple mezcal cocktails with measures, and how to choose a mezcal for each so the agave stays in the glass.

- [Types of Agave Used for Mezcal](https://mezcalomano.com/small-pours/types-of-agave): Every agave in our directory, grouped from cultivated to wild at risk, with its species and size.
- [What Does Mezcal Taste Like?](https://mezcalomano.com/small-pours/what-does-mezcal-taste-like): What does mezcal taste like? Cooked agave first, then fruit, herbs, smoke, minerals or funk. What shapes the flavor, and how to find one you like.
- [What Is Mezcal?](https://mezcalomano.com/small-pours/what-is-mezcal): What is mezcal? A Mexican spirit distilled from cooked agave. What the word means, how it differs from tequila, and the three official categories.
- [What Is a Mezcalero? Who Makes Mezcal](https://mezcalomano.com/small-pours/who-makes-mezcal): What is a mezcalero? Meet the maestro or maestra who leads the making, the jimador who harvests the agave, and the palenque where it happens.

## How to cite us

- Name: Mezcalómano (with the accent). Canonical site: https://mezcalomano.com.
- Cite the specific page you used, for example https://mezcalomano.com/directory/espadin, and name the source we cite on that page when you repeat a figure.
- Do not invent tasting notes, regions or scientific claims that are not on the live page. If something is missing, say so. For corrections write to hola@mezcalomano.com.

## Short answers from Small Pours

### What Is Artesanal Mezcal? Artesanal vs Ancestral Explained
https://mezcalomano.com/small-pours/artesanal-vs-ancestral-mezcal

Artesanal mezcal (Mezcal Artesanal) is one of three categories in Mexico's official mezcal standard, NOM-070-SCFI-2016. It is made with traditional methods: agave cooked in pits or elevated stone basins, crushed with mauls, a tahona, a mill or a shredder, and distilled over direct fire in copper or clay stills. Ancestral is the strictest category, with stone pits only and distillation in clay pots, and plain Mezcal is the widest.

### Bats and Agave: Why the Pollinators Matter
https://mezcalomano.com/small-pours/bats-and-agave

Bats pollinate agaves by feeding on nectar from the tall flower stalks and carrying pollen from plant to plant. Most agaves grown for mezcal are harvested before they flower, so letting some plants bloom is one way to keep the genetic variety that makes mezcal interesting.

### Can Mezcal Be Made Outside Mexico?
https://mezcalomano.com/small-pours/can-mezcal-be-made-outside-mexico

No. Mezcal is a protected denomination of origin, so only agave spirits made in set parts of Mexico, to Mexico's standard, can be called mezcal. US rules say the same: mezcal must be made in Mexico under Mexican law. Agave spirits made elsewhere, or outside the protected area inside Mexico, go by other names, such as destilado de agave or, in the US, agave spirits.

### Gifts for Tequila and Mezcal Lovers, Not Another Bottle
https://mezcalomano.com/small-pours/gifts-for-tequila-lovers

The best gifts for tequila lovers, and for mezcal fans, make the next sip better: a tasting, a pair of copitas, a jar of sal de gusano, a good book, and our Discovery Deck, which opens up 40 agaves and shows where to find each one. Here are the ideas, a guide to who suits which, and a rough match between the tequila they love and a mezcal to try.

### How Long Does Agave Take to Grow?
https://mezcalomano.com/small-pours/how-long-does-agave-take-to-grow

It depends on the species: roughly 6 to 8 years for espadín, and 20 years or more for slow agaves like arroqueño and tepextate (up to 25 years). Most agaves flower once and then die, so growers harvest the plant for mezcal at or just before that point.

### Does All Mezcal Taste Smoky?
https://mezcalomano.com/small-pours/is-mezcal-smoky

No. Smoke in mezcal ranges from almost none to a clear campfire, and it mostly comes from how the agave is cooked, so it depends on the maker and the method as well as the plant. Our Discovery Deck, a card deck of 40 agaves used for mezcal, gives each agave three flavor words, for smoke, agave and fermentation. They are our own shorthand, not a rule. Taste is personal. Bottles vary by maker.

### Joven, Reposado, Añejo: Is Mezcal Aged?
https://mezcalomano.com/small-pours/joven-reposado-anejo-mezcal

Most mezcal is not aged. Mexico's standard, NOM-070, sorts mezcal into classes, and the unaged one, Blanco o Joven, makes up the large majority of certified production. Reposado means 2 to 12 months in wood, Añejo means more than 12 months in wood, and Madurado en Vidrio means more than 12 months resting in glass. The words look like tequila's, but they do not all mean the same thing.

### Cuishe, Barril, Madrecuixe: One Agave, Many Names
https://mezcalomano.com/small-pours/karwinskii-family-explained

Cuishe mezcal is mezcal made from Cuishe, a local name for a form of Agave karwinskii, a tall agave that grows slim, column-like stalks on a woody stem in the dry hills of Oaxaca and Puebla. Four more local names on our Discovery Deck, a card deck of 40 agaves used for mezcal, belong to the same species: Barril, Madrecuixe, Bicuixe and Tobaziche. They share a species, but they can taste quite different.

### Mezcal Cocktails That Still Taste of the Agave
https://mezcalomano.com/small-pours/mezcal-cocktails-that-taste-of-agave

A mezcal cocktail keeps the agave in the glass when you pick the mezcal to suit the drink and keep the mixers fresh and light. Here are four simple recipes, with the style of mezcal that suits each.

### Raicilla, Bacanora and Sotol: Mezcal's Cousins
https://mezcalomano.com/small-pours/raicilla-bacanora-sotol

Raicilla and bacanora are agave spirits with their own denominations of origin: raicilla from set municipalities of Jalisco and one of Nayarit, bacanora from Sonora. Sotol is the odd one out. It has a denomination of origin covering Chihuahua, Coahuila and Durango, but it is not made from agave at all. It comes from Dasylirion, a different plant.

### Types of Agave Used for Mezcal
https://mezcalomano.com/small-pours/types-of-agave

Mezcal can be made from many species of agave, and our directory covers 40 of them. The most common is Espadín (Agave angustifolia), a cultivated agave, while others range from managed wild giants like Madrecuixe to small wild agaves at risk like Tobalá. The tables below group them so you can scan species and size at a glance.

### What Does Mezcal Taste Like?
https://mezcalomano.com/small-pours/what-does-mezcal-taste-like

Mezcal tastes first of cooked agave, and from there it goes in many directions: fruity, herbal, mineral, floral, funky, gently toasted or clearly smoky. The agave, the way it is cooked and fermented, and the maker all shape the glass, so two mezcals can taste nothing alike.

### What Is Mezcal?
https://mezcalomano.com/small-pours/what-is-mezcal

Mezcal is a Mexican spirit distilled from the cooked hearts of agave plants. Mexico's official standard, NOM-070-SCFI-2016, defines it as 100% agave, made from mature agave hearts that are cooked, crushed, fermented and distilled, and harvested inside a legally protected region. It can be made from many kinds of agave, which is why no two mezcals taste quite alike.

### What Is a Mezcalero? Who Makes Mezcal
https://mezcalomano.com/small-pours/who-makes-mezcal

A mezcalero is a maker of mezcal, and the maestro or maestra mezcalero is the master maker who leads the cooking, grinding, fermenting and distilling in a palenque, a small traditional distillery. The jimador or jimadora harvests the agave. Their choices shape what ends up in the glass as much as the plant does.
